UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
V. Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
The Honorable Judge

Rossie D. Alston Jr.

KATIE HALL, individually;

NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;

and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

Defendants.

PLAINTIFF’S PROPOSED SUPPLEMENTAL COMPLAINT TO FIRST AMENDED
COMPLAINT
PURSUANT TO FED. R. CIV. P. 15(d)

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine, pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d),
supplements Count III of the operative First Amended Complaint with events occurring after that
pleading was filed. The First Amended Complaint remains unchanged. This Supplemental
Complaint adds no defendant, no cause of action, and no category of relief, and is directed solely to
Count III.

I. INCORPORATION AND SCOPE
1. Plaintiff incorporates by reference the allegations in the Preliminary Statement,

Jurisdiction and Venue, Parties, and Scope of Allegations sections of the First Amended

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 26-1 Filed 08/21/26 Page 2 of 8 PagelD#
303

Complaint; Sections A, B, C, G, H, I, J, M, and R of the Facts of the First Amended Complaint; and
Count III of the First Amended Complaint, as if fully set forth herein.

2. The allegations below supplement Count III only. They concern post-filing
knowledge, state of mind, acknowledged distress, continuation of the course of conduct alleged in
Count III, and Defendants’ present awareness that the person-level uncertainty created by the April
22, 2026 letters remains unresolved.

3. No independent cause of action is predicated on the filing of NCMEC’s August 12,
2026 memorandum or on the August 13, 2026 communication alleged below. Consistent with the
Scope of Allegations section of the First Amended Complaint, those post-filing events are alleged
solely as facts bearing on knowledge, state of mind, intent or recklessness, continuation of the
conduct alleged in Count III, and awareness of continuing injury.

II. POST-FILING EVENTS

4. On August 12, 2026, NCMEC filed its memorandum in support of its motion to
dismiss the First Amended Complaint. ECF No. 11. The memorandum was filed on behalf of
NCMEC and stated that, unless otherwise specified, its arguments applied equally to Defendant
Hall because she was at all relevant times an employee of NCMEC.

5. NCMEC’s August 12, 2026 memorandum expressly addressed the First Amended
Complaint’s allegations that Plaintiff is a survivor of childhood sexual abuse; that, after receiving
the April 22, 2026 letters, Plaintiff vomited; that Plaintiff experienced recollections of childhood
sexual abuse; and that Plaintiff experienced fear of arrest and prosecution.

6. By August 12, 2026, NCMEC had actual knowledge of Plaintiff’s disclosed survivor
history and of the severe emotional distress Plaintiff alleged resulted from the April 22, 2026

letters.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 26-1 Filed 08/21/26 Page 3 of 8 PagelD#
304

7. Inaddressing Plaintiff’s falsity allegations, NCMEC’s August 12, 2026 memorandum
stated both that Plaintiff “does not have access to those reports” and that the asserted CyberTipline
linkage could concern Plaintiff, “a person with the same name,” or an email address.

8. NCMEC thereby acknowledged that the April 22, 2026 letters did not resolve whether
either asserted CyberTipline report concerned Plaintiff personally, another person with the same
name, or an email identifier.

9. NCMEC possesses the two CyberTipline reports underlying the April 22, 2026 letters.

10. Plaintiff does not possess or have access to those reports.

11. The April 22, 2026 letters do not identify which listed person or identifier
corresponds to either report.

12. As of August 12, 2026, the resulting person-level uncertainty remained unresolved
from Plaintiff’s perspective.

13. NCMEC knew that the uncertainty remained unresolved.

14. On August 13, 2026, Plaintiff sought clarification concerning the unresolved identity
question by asking counsel for NCMEC and Hall whether either CyberTipline report, as received
from the reporting provider, contained or identified: (1) Plaintiff’s full legal name, “Marvelle J.
Ballentine”; (2) the name “Jay Ballentine”; or (3) the email identifier jaychizza@icloud.com.

15. Counsel did not provide an answer resolving whether any of those identifiers
appeared in either provider-submitted report.

16. On August 13, 2026, one day after NCMEC filed its memorandum, counsel
representing NCMEC and Hall wrote to Plaintiff: “I read your email as being upset with the
language used in the memorandum—I did not intend to offend you with the phrasing, but my point

was you got exactly what you asked for, using the language you provided.”

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 26-1 Filed 08/21/26 Page 4 of 8 PagelD#
305

17. When counsel made the August 13, 2026 statement: NCMEC had demonstrated
actual knowledge of Plaintiff’s survivor history and of the emotional injuries pleaded in the First
Amended Complaint; counsel expressly acknowledged that Plaintiff was upset; the April 22, 2026
letters remained unretracted and uncorrected; NCMEC continued to possess the two underlying
CyberTipline reports; Plaintiff continued to lack access to those reports; and the person-level
uncertainty described in NCMEC’s August 12, 2026 memorandum remained unresolved.

18. The unresolved question whether either asserted CyberTipline report concerns
Plaintiff personally remained a continuing consequence of the April 22, 2026 letters after the filing
of the First Amended Complaint and continued to sustain the apprehension alleged in Count III.

Ill. SUPPLEMENT TO COUNT III
INTENTIONAL INFLICTION OF EMOTIONAL DISTRESS
(Against Defendants Katie Hall and NCMEC)

19. Plaintiff incorporates the preceding allegations of this Supplemental Complaint and
the allegations incorporated into Count III of the First Amended Complaint as though fully set forth
herein.

20. By August 12, 2026, NCMEC had actual knowledge of Plaintiff’s disclosed survivor
history and of the severe emotional distress Plaintiff alleged the April 22, 2026 letters caused. The
following day, counsel representing NCMEC and Hall acknowledged that Plaintiff was upset and
stated that Plaintiff “got exactly what you asked for, using the language you provided.”

21. The post-filing sequence — actual knowledge of the pleaded injuries,
acknowledgment of Plaintiff’s distress, continued possession of the information capable of
resolving the person-level uncertainty, continued knowledge that Plaintiff lacked access to that

information, and the August 13, 2026 statement — further supports Count III’s existing allegations

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 26-1 Filed 08/21/26 Page 5 of 8 PagelD#
306

that the course of conduct was intentional or reckless and was continued with knowledge of its
effect on Plaintiff.

22. NCMEC also knew that Plaintiff lacked access to the reports and that the April 22,
2026 letters had left unresolved whether either asserted report concemed Plaintiff personally,
another person with the same name, or an email identifier. Because that uncertainty remained
unresolved, the apprehension alleged in Count III continued after the filing of the First Amended
Complaint. Considered with the conduct already alleged in Count III, the post-filing events further
support the existing allegations concerning intent or recklessness, outrageousness, and continuing
injury.

IV. RELIEF

This Supplemental Complaint seeks no relief different from or additional to the relief
requested under Count III of the First Amended Complaint. Plaintiff respectfully requests that the
Court read this Supplemental Complaint together with the operative First Amended Complaint and

award the relief requested therein.
